method: monotone word-overlap difflib; heuristic, not semantic proof

units.source_text: Handle whatever safety issue or practical thing actually needs doing. Then, before another round, ask what changed the last time you processed this.
units.output_text: Do whatever it is that needs to be done (usually this will be safety related).

units.source_text: Did you finally feel something you had only been thinking about?
units.output_text: At the start of the next round of processing, ask yourself why you are here again. Why has something changed since you were last here?

units.source_text: Did you notice something new enough to change a decision or how you respond? Or are you asking the same question again because the answer didn't feel certain enough?
units.output_text: Has something come up that allows you to deal with this differently now, or has something come up that makes you unsure of your last answer?

units.source_text: Grief can come back to familiar ground. Repetition by itself doesn't mean the child has a new request.
units.output_text: Grief does often repeat itself, and that doesn't mean that the child is asking for something new.
